items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: Martha Turner & Dave Allen had pianos, see, and I used to go and play that

ctx.x: And I had an opportunity to see Daybreak Nelson, who was a comedian, and some dancers and some singers... early singers of that period. Finally the time came that my mother decided to move to Dallas. She went ahead and got a little house for us and in 1918 we moved to Dallas. Well, I got right off the Inter-Urban and went straight to the Park Theater to find Ella B. Moore. Now I didn't have any idea that Mrs. Moore would have anything to do, Danny, with my playing music. You know, because in those days you were…

let me practice on your piano." Just like that. Now, that was my introduction...those were the first words spoken, you know, about the piano. She says, "Okay, some Saturday morning." And I came Saturday morning and I worked hard and finally the time came for me to go into this lady's parlor and sit down at the piano. Well, what I did was to play the piano roll and watch where the notes went down and then sequels like that, and I learned how to play a song called, "My Isle of Golden Dreams." That's how I learned…
